binary-search__median-of-two-sorted-arra.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
binary-search__median-of-two-sorted-arra.statement: Given two sorted arrays `nums1`, `nums2`, return the median of the combined array in **O(log(m+n))**.

approaches.name: Partition the smaller array
approaches.idea: Binary-search a cut `i` in the smaller array; the cut `j` in the other is fixed by `j = half - i`. A valid partition satisfies `left1 <= right2 && left2 <= right1`. Use `+/-inf` sentinels for out-of-range edges. `half = (m+n+1)/2` makes the odd case just `max(left1,left2)`.

binary-search__median-of-two-sorted-arra.insight: Search the partition point of the shorter array; the other partition is derived. Valid cut iff `max(lefts) <= min(rights)` across the two arrays.

binary-search__koko-eating-bananas.title: Koko Eating Bananas
binary-search__koko-eating-bananas.pattern: Binary search on the answer (min feasible speed)
binary-search__koko-eating-bananas.statement: Koko eats bananas from `piles`. Each hour she picks one pile and eats up to `k` bananas from it (if the pile has fewer, she finishes it and stops for that hour). Given `h` hours, return the **minimum** integer eating speed `k` such that she finishes all piles within `h` hours.

approaches.name: Binary search on speed
approaches.idea: `hoursNeeded(k)` is monotonically non-increasing in `k`. Search `k` in `[1, max(piles)]` for the smallest `k` with `hoursNeeded(k) <= h`. Hours for a pile at speed `k` is `ceil(pile/k)`.

binary-search__koko-eating-bananas.insight: Feasibility is monotonic in the guessed speed, so binary-search the smallest feasible speed. Use `ceil` via `(p + k - 1)/k`.

binary-search__capacity-to-ship-packages.title: Capacity to Ship Packages Within D Days
binary-search__capacity-to-ship-packages.pattern: Binary search on the answer (min capacity)
binary-search__capacity-to-ship-packages.statement: Packages on a conveyor must ship in `days` days, in order. Each day the ship carries a contiguous prefix of remaining packages without exceeding its capacity. Return the least ship capacity to finish within `days`.

approaches.name: Binary search on capacity
approaches.idea: Lower bound = `max(weights)` (a package must fit); upper bound = `sum(weights)` (ship it all in one day). `daysNeeded(cap)` is non-increasing in `cap`. Find the smallest `cap` needing `<= days`.

binary-search__capacity-to-ship-packages.insight: Same skeleton as Koko. The only judgement is the search bounds: `[max element, total sum]`. Identical in structure to Split Array Largest Sum.

binary-search__split-array-largest-sum.title: Split Array Largest Sum
binary-search__split-array-largest-sum.pattern: Binary search on the answer (minimize max subarray sum)
binary-search__split-array-largest-sum.statement: Split `nums` into `k` non-empty contiguous subarrays to **minimize the largest** subarray sum. Return that minimized largest sum.

approaches.name: Binary search on the answer
approaches.idea: This is exactly Capacity to Ship Packages with `days = k`: find the smallest cap so the array can be cut into `<= k` pieces each with sum `<= cap`. Bounds `[max, sum]`.

approaches.name: DP over cuts
approaches.idea: `dp[i][j]` = min possible largest sum splitting the first `i` elements into `j` parts; transition over the last cut using prefix sums. `O(n^2 k)` time, strictly worse; use only when the answer is not monotonic-checkable.

binary-search__split-array-largest-sum.insight: "Minimize the maximum" over contiguous splits => binary search the answer; feasibility check = greedy count of pieces. Ship-packages / split-array / painter's partition are the same problem.

binary-search__find-minimum-in-rotated-s.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array II
binary-search__find-minimum-in-rotated-s.statement: A sorted array (may contain **duplicates**) was rotated. Return the minimum element.

approaches.name: Compare mid with hi
approaches.idea: Compare `nums[mid]` to `nums[hi]`: if `> nums[hi]` the min is strictly right (`lo = mid+1`); if `< nums[hi]` the min is at mid or left (`hi = mid`); if `== nums[hi]` we cannot tell, so shrink safely with `hi--` (the element at `hi` is duplicated by `mid`, so dropping it is safe).
approaches.time: O(log n) average, O(n) worst (all equal)

binary-search__find-minimum-in-rotated-s.insight: Compare to `hi`, not `lo` (comparing to `lo` breaks on non-rotated arrays). Duplicates force the `hi--` fallback, which pushes worst case to O(n).

binary-search__find-k-th-smallest-pair-d.title: Find K-th Smallest Pair Distance
binary-search__find-k-th-smallest-pair-d.pattern: Binary search on the answer + two-pointer counting
binary-search__find-k-th-smallest-pair-d.statement: Given `nums`, the distance of a pair `(i,j)` is `|nums[i]-nums[j]|`. Return the **k-th smallest** distance among all pairs.

approaches.name: Binary search on distance, count pairs <= mid
approaches.idea: Sort. `countLE(d)` = number of pairs with distance `<= d`, computed with a sliding window in O(n) (for each right, advance left while `nums[right]-nums[left] > d`, add `right-left`). The count is non-decreasing in `d`; find the smallest `d` with `count(d) >= k`.

binary-search__find-k-th-smallest-pair-d.insight: Search over the distance value, not indices. The feasibility check ("how many pairs <= d") is itself a two-pointer O(n) count: pairs-with-distance => sort + sliding window.

binary-search__kth-smallest-element-in-a.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
binary-search__kth-smallest-element-in-a.pattern: Binary search on value in a row/col-sorted matrix
binary-search__kth-smallest-element-in-a.statement: `n x n` matrix with rows and columns sorted ascending. Return the k-th smallest element (in sorted order, counting duplicates).

approaches.name: Binary search on value
approaches.idea: Search value in `[matrix[0][0], matrix[n-1][n-1]]`. `countLE(x)` walks from bottom-left: move right when `<= x` (add whole column above+self), else move up. The smallest `x` with `countLE(x) >= k` is an actual matrix value.

approaches.name: Min-heap of size n
approaches.idea: Push the first element of each row; pop `k` times, pushing the next element in the popped element's row. `O(k log n)`. Simpler to reason about but slower for large k.

binary-search__kth-smallest-element-in-a.insight: Do not heap-merge unless k is small. The staircase `countLE` (start bottom-left) turns "sorted matrix" into a 1-D binary-search-on-value.

binary-search__minimize-max-distance-to-.title: Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station
binary-search__minimize-max-distance-to-.pattern: Binary search on a real-valued answer
binary-search__minimize-max-distance-to-.statement: Given sorted positions `stations` of existing gas stations on a horizontal line and an integer `k`, add `k` new stations (anywhere, integer not required) to minimize the maximum distance between adjacent stations. Return that minimized maximum distance; answers within `1e-6` of the true value are accepted.

examples.explanation: Add one station in the middle of each unit gap.

constraints: stations is sorted in strictly increasing order

approaches.name: Binary search on the max distance
approaches.idea: Guess a candidate max distance `d` (a real number). For each existing gap `g = stations[i]-stations[i-1]`, the minimum new stations needed to keep every sub-gap `<= d` is `floor(g/d)`; sum these. The requirement is monotonic: larger `d` needs fewer stations, so it is feasible iff `total <= k`. Binary-search `d` in `[0, maxGap]` until the window is below `1e-6`.

binary-search__minimize-max-distance-to-.insight: "Minimize the maximum" with a continuous answer => binary-search on a real value with an epsilon stop; feasibility of gap `d` is `sum(floor(gap/d)) <= k`.

binary-search__aggressive-cows-magnetic-.title: Aggressive Cows / Magnetic Force Between Balls
binary-search__aggressive-cows-magnetic-.pattern: Binary search on the answer (maximize the minimum gap)
binary-search__aggressive-cows-magnetic-.statement: Given distinct integer positions `position` of `n` baskets and `m` balls, place all `m` balls into baskets so that the **minimum** distance between any two balls is as large as possible. Return that maximized minimum distance. (Equivalent to Aggressive Cows: place `m` cows in stalls maximizing the closest pair.)

examples.explanation: Place balls at 1, 4, 7; the minimum pairwise distance is 3.

approaches.name: Binary search on the minimum gap + greedy check
approaches.idea: Sort positions. Guess a minimum gap `d`; greedily place a ball at the leftmost basket, then at each next basket at least `d` away from the last placed ball. Feasibility is monotonic: a larger `d` fits fewer balls, so it is feasible iff we can place `>= m` balls. Binary-search the largest feasible `d` in `[1, maxPos-minPos]`.

binary-search__aggressive-cows-magnetic-.insight: "Maximize the minimum" => binary-search the gap; the check is a greedy left-to-right placement counting how many balls fit with spacing `>= d`.

binary-search__median-of-a-row-wise-sort.title: Median of a Row-Wise Sorted Matrix
binary-search__median-of-a-row-wise-sort.pattern: Binary search on value + per-row upper bound counting
binary-search__median-of-a-row-wise-sort.statement: Given an `r x c` matrix where **each row is sorted** in ascending order and `r*c` is odd, return the median of all `r*c` elements. Rows are independent (columns are NOT necessarily sorted), and the goal is better than the `O(r*c)` full-materialization approach.

examples.explanation: Sorted elements: 1,2,3,3,5,6,6,9,9; the middle (5th) element is 5.

constraints: each row of matrix is sorted ascending

approaches.name: Binary search on value with row upper-bounds
approaches.idea: The median is the smallest value `v` such that the count of elements `<= v` exceeds `(r*c)/2`. Binary-search `v` in `[min of first column, max of last column]`; for each candidate, count elements `<= v` by summing an upper-bound binary search over every sorted row. Move `hi = mid` when the count exceeds `need`, else `lo = mid+1`. The final `lo` is a real matrix element (the median).

binary-search__median-of-a-row-wise-sort.insight: Median = smallest value whose "count of elements <= it" exceeds half; binary-search the value and count per row with an upper bound instead of merging all rows.
